effect_estimate.comment: Reports both longitudinal latrine construction coverage, cross-arm awareness comparisons from the cluster-randomised villages, and village-level linear regression coefficients within the 50 intervention villages alongside qualitative implementation findings.
effect_estimate.value: Latrine coverage (completed or under construction) in the 50 intervention villages increased from 8% at baseline (October 2010) to 66% in March 2012 (68% among BPL households vs. 61% among APL households; range 54% to 76% across NGOs), while completed latrine coverage rose from 8% to 51% between January 2011 and January 2012 (below the 90% target). In the random 10% household survey (n = 807: 408 intervention, 399 control), intervention households had higher awareness of the Total Sanitation Campaign (91% vs. 49%, p < 0.001), VWSCs (51% vs. 9%, p < 0.001), adolescent girls groups (23% vs. 8%, p < 0.01), wall paintings (44% vs. 7%, p < 0.001), and sanitation home visits in the past 3 months (65% vs. 3%, p < 0.001), but negligible recall of participatory transect walks/mapping (6% vs. 10%, p = 0.04) or wealth ranking (0% vs. 1%, p = 0.09). In village-level linear regressions across the 50 intervention villages, latrine coverage was associated with seeing wall paintings (beta = 0.171, 95% CI: 0.001 to 0.341, p = 0.05), a village motivator home visit in the past month (beta = 0.216, 95% CI: -0.000 to 0.431, p = 0.05 in Table 4; p = 0.02 in text), and >=5 VWSC meetings held (beta = 0.178, 95% CI: 0.010 to 0.346, p = 0.04), with no significant association for participatory mobilisation activities; restricting subsidies to BPL/wealth-ranked poor households caused community tensions that led implementers to extend subsidies to all intervention households.

mechanism_certainty.comment: Mixed-methods process evaluation (appraised with MMAT, design ceiling = 2) that directly observed and documented administrative and implementation mechanisms on the ground, including BPL list verification, community tensions over selective poverty-targeted subsidies prompting discretionary universal subsidy extension, complaints following the statutory subsidy raise from Rs 2200 to Rs 3200, VWSC functioning, NGO motivator visits, and election code-of-conduct halts.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines BPL card eligibility verification against Gram Panchayat records (ELIGIBILITY, documentation), wealth-ranking and WaterAid subsidies for non-BPL poor plus discretionary extension of INR 2200 subsidies to all households to avert conflict (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, hardship_exception, discretion), household co-contributions of ~INR 2200 in materials/labour (BURDEN, fees), implementation delays (delay), community complaints over the subsidy increase from Rs 2200 to Rs 3200 and construction disputes (complaint), VWSCs and PRA mobilisation (participation), NGO-local government coordination and 2-month election code-of-conduct halts/local political unrest (political_coordination), and weekly door-to-door NGO village motivator support with construction logistics (bureaucratic_assistance).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Although embedded within a 100-village cluster-randomised trial (whose trial protocol and main health trial are reported separately), this paper is a mixed-methods process evaluation combining primary qualitative methods (semi-structured interviews with NGO staff/motivators and community members, review of implementation logs/documents) and primary quantitative methods (repeated direct observations of household latrines, random household and VWSC surveys, and observational village-level linear regressions in the 50 intervention villages), making MMAT the design-matched appraisal tool.

sample_size.comment: Multiple nested samples are explicitly reported for the different components of the mixed-methods process evaluation within the 100-village trial.
sample_size.value: 100 villages (50 intervention villages and 50 control villages); latrine construction observations in 4,699 households (March 2012) and 4,585 households (March 2013); household awareness survey of 807 households (408 intervention and 399 control, 10% random sample); VWSC survey of 170 village water and sanitation committee members across intervention villages (VWSC composition data from 48 villages); plus semi-structured interviews and logbook reviews with NGO staff (25 village motivators and 6 cluster coordinators trained)

study_design.comment: Process evaluation conducted alongside a cluster-randomised trial, based on the Linnan and Steckler framework, integrating qualitative interviews/document review with quantitative household and VWSC surveys, direct latrine observations every 6-8 weeks, cross-arm t-tests of village proportions, and observational village-level linear regression.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods process evaluation conducted in connection with a cluster-randomised controlled trial (combining document review, semi-structured interviews, longitudinal direct observations of latrine construction, cross-sectional household and VWSC member surveys, and village-level linear regression)
